title: Characterisation of blood cell aggregates in viral and bacterial ARDS using digital holographic microscopy
summary: Bacteria and viruses can cause pneumonia that, in some cases, requires mechanical ventilation and treatment on an intensive care unit. The underlying factors determining the severity of the disease have not been well understood. Preliminary studies were able to correlate blood cell and blood cell aggregate alterations with disease severity. We have developed a microscopic method that allows to detect and analyze blood cells and cell aggregates without staining or preparation steps. Further, we can measure messengers released from artificially stimulated blood cells of patients to study immunological responses. In this study, we will apply both methods to investigate blood cells and aggregates in patients with severe pneumonia. Comparing our data with clinical data, we aim to determine whether blood cell aggregates are suitable as diagnostic or prognostic markers in pneumonia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- mechanical ventilation
- meeting the criteria of one of the following subgroups (retrospective re-assignment possible)
1. bacterial ARDS (according to Berlin-Definition of ARDS and typical radiological finding or pathogen detected in respiratory specimen)
2. viral ARDS (according to Berlin-Definition of ARDS and molecular detection in respiratory specimen)
3. lack of viral/bacterial infection and no evidence of systemic infection in clinically/laboratory investigation
Exclusion criteria:
- allocation to one of the subgroups impossible
